title: Verify Fargate cannot host a WireGuard peer
description:
## Question

**Can ECS Fargate host a WireGuard peer?**

`chatticus-fbae4e` D2 asserts it cannot — Fargate supports neither privileged mode nor `NET_ADMIN` / `/dev/net/tun` — and marks the claim *"verify before implementation."*

This is a **documentation check, not a spike.** Recorded as a task so nobody spends a day building a Fargate-based tunnel endpoint on an unverified assumption, and so nobody spends a day *proving* something a doc page settles in minutes.

## Why it matters

If the assertion is wrong and Fargate *can* run a WireGuard peer, the tunnel endpoint becomes scale-to-zero rather than a stopped-when-idle EC2 instance. That drops the idle floor from ~$0.65/mo to $0 and removes a box to patch — a genuine improvement to D2, not a rounding error, given the initiative's cost argument turns on idle floors.

If the assertion is right, D2 stands as written and the "verify" caveat comes out.

## How

Check the ECS task definition documentation for `linuxParameters.capabilities.add` support on the Fargate launch type, and for privileged mode. If ambiguous, attempt a task definition requesting `NET_ADMIN` and observe whether registration or task start is rejected.

## Cost

Minutes.

## Done when

`chatticus-fbae4e` D2 either drops its "verify before implementation" caveat, or is corrected along with the endpoint cost figures that depend on it.
